sources.note: Nothing; lists 'Yiddish Sign Language [yds] – no evidence that it existed', citing CR 2014-010.

sources.citation: Bickford, J. Albert (with Bernard Spolsky, Bar-Ilan Univ.). 2014. ISO 639-3 Change Request 2014-010: Retire [yds] Yiddish Sign Language (adopted 2015-01-12). SIL International, 6 pp.
sources.note: Nothing about stress; it is a retirement request. Reason ticked: 'There is no evidence that the language exists.' (p.2, sec. 3a). Quotes Spolsky: 'There are no published descriptions or detailed attestations of its existence' (p.2, 3d); 'a distinct unified Yiddish Sign Language is unattested and unlikely' (p.3, 3g). Ethnologue entry traced to a footnote in Oliver Sacks 1990 Seeing Voices; Ethnologue reclassified it 'unattested'.

sources.citation: Spolsky, Bernard. 2014 (last update 2014-01-24). 'Yiddish Sign Language.' Jewish Language Research Website (ed. Sarah Bunin Benor). Original URL now 404; Internet Archive copy read.
sources.note: Nothing about stress. Primary text behind the ISO retirement: no published descriptions; experts (W. Sandler, B. Woll, N. Brunlehrman, B. Weiser) have not heard of it; 'a distinct unified Yiddish Sign Language is unattested and unlikely.'
